A distance of about \(2.1\ \mathrm{Gpc}\) corresponds to a redshift of roughly \(z\sim 0.5\). The rest-frame energy is therefore

\[
E_{\rm rest}=E_{\rm obs}(1+z)
\approx (3.9\times10^{-6}\,\mathrm{eV})(1.5)
\approx 5.9\times10^{-6}\,\mathrm{eV}.
\]

This is the energy of the neutral hydrogen \(21\)-cm hyperfine line. In absorption, the \(21\)-cm line preferentially traces cold neutral atomic hydrogen, so in the Milky Way it is most associated with the **cold atomic interstellar medium**.

Answer: C
